questions.q: How does SQL Server Profiler differ from Chapter 10's execution plan and STATISTICS tools?
options: It only works on Azure SQL Database, never on-premises
It replaces the need for indexes entirely
It can only be used before a query runs, never during or after
It watches the entire server in real time, capturing every query from every session, instead of analyzing one query you already picked
questions.explain: Profiler is for the situation where you don't yet know which query is the problem — it observes everything happening server-wide.

questions.q: What does a Profiler trace event capture?
options: A screenshot of the SSMS window
The physical disk layout of the server
Only the names of tables in the database
Details like the T-SQL text, duration, CPU, logical reads/writes, login name, and database
questions.explain: Each trace row records one event with metrics similar to STATISTICS TIME/IO, but for any query running anywhere on the server.

questions.q: What is the status of SQL Server Profiler today?
options: It was renamed but functions identically
It only works with SQL Server Express edition
Deprecated, along with the underlying SQL Trace feature
It's the newest, most recommended diagnostic tool
questions.explain: Microsoft has officially deprecated both SQL Server Profiler and SQL Trace.

questions.q: What is the modern replacement for SQL Server Profiler?
options: SET STATISTICS PROFILE
There is no replacement — tracing is no longer possible
Extended Events, accessible in SSMS through the XEvent Profiler
The Database Engine Tuning Advisor
questions.explain: Extended Events is the lighter-weight tracing engine that replaces the deprecated Profiler/SQL Trace combination.

questions.q: When would you reach for a server-wide trace instead of Chapter 10's per-query tools?
options: Only when working with AdventureWorksDW2014, never AdventureWorks2012
Never — Chapter 10's tools always replace the need for a trace
When a problem is server-wide and undiagnosed — you don't yet know which specific query is causing the slowdown
Every single time you write a new query, before running it even once
questions.explain: A trace helps narrow down an unknown, server-wide problem to the one statement worth analyzing further with Chapter 10's tools.
